text:
yun: Noticed sampleapp memory creep after switching to dedicated OkHttp client for token refresh. Emulator network sockets keep piling up.

max: Logs? leak trace?

yun: Quick dump: 

W/System.err: java.net.SocketException: socket failed: EMFILE (Too many open files)
at okhttp3.internal.connection.RealConnection.connect(RealConnection.kt:...)
...

max: Huh. We added a short-lived OkHttpClient for refresh in TokenProvider, but maybe we never evict its connection pool. Can you paste the provider snippet?

yun: Sure (simplified):

```kotlin
object TokenProvider {
  fun refreshBlocking(): String {
    val client = OkHttpClient.Builder().build() // created per-refresh
    val req = Request.Builder().url("https://auth/refresh").post(body).build()
    client.newCall(req).execute().use { resp -> return resp.body!!.string() }
  }
}
```

rita: There's the smell. Creating a new OkHttpClient per refresh without shutting down its dispatcher/connection pool leads to idle connections piling up. On Android the platform cap for fds causes EMFILE over time.

yun: I assumed Garbage Collection would close things. Apparently not quick enough.

max: Two immediate fixes: reuse a single dedicated client for refreshes (singleton) or explicitly call client.connectionPool.evictAll() and client.dispatcher.executorService.shutdown() after finished. Prefer reuse.

rita: Also note: using client.newCall().execute() inside a long-lived thread can block; prefer using that dedicated client's dispatcher config (small pool) and schedule tasks on it instead of spinning up clients.

yun: I switched to a single lazy val refreshClient and updated the provider to reuse it. After a 24h soak locally, EMFILE didn't reproduce.

max: Great. Add a comment in sampleapp showing the wrong vs right pattern. Also add a linter rule in devex checklist: "Don't create OkHttpClient per request."

rita: This also matters for warmup: if you create many clients you get many connection pools, worse for mobile. Document the eviction API and the executor shutdown pattern for people who really need ephemeral clients.

yun: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/pull/960 with the fix and a small integration test that creates 500 sequential refreshes on emulator.

ci-bot: Created issue #4412: "OkHttp client-per-refresh causes socket FD leak in sampleapp" - https://git.internal/redwood/issues/4412 :warning:

max: Add a short blurb to the onboarding guide about preferred token refresh patterns and the connection-pool cost. I'll fold it into the v0.13 migration notes.

yun: Thanks all, leaving this thread. Will follow up if CI flaps.
